recipes.title: Akara, light
recipes.summary: Crisp West African black-eyed pea fritters with a soft, savoury centre. Extra bell pepper and less oil keep this shared snack lighter without changing its character.

steps.instruction: Pat the cowpeas dry so the fritter batter will not become watery.
Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic into pieces small enough for the blender.
Blend the cowpeas, onion, bell pepper, garlic, ginger, cayenne pepper, water and salt into a thick, slightly textured batter.
Beat the batter vigorously until it looks lighter and holds soft peaks.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Fry spoonfuls of batter until golden and firm on both sides, working in batches.
Drain the akara briefly on absorbent paper.
Rest the akara until cool enough to eat while the crust finishes setting.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served warm and freshly fried. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a hot oven or dry pan. Freeze cooked akara for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Akara
recipes.summary: Golden West African black-eyed pea fritters blended with onion, pepper, garlic and ginger. They are crisp outside, fluffy within and made for sharing.

steps.instruction: Pat the cowpeas dry so the fritter batter will stay thick.
Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic into pieces small enough for the blender.
Blend the cowpeas, onion, bell pepper, garlic, ginger, cayenne pepper, water and salt into a thick, slightly textured batter.
Beat the batter vigorously until it becomes airy and holds soft peaks.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Fry spoonfuls of batter until deeply golden and cooked through, working in batches.
Drain the akara briefly on absorbent paper.
Rest the akara until cool enough to eat and the crust feels crisp.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve warm for the best crisp texture. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a hot oven or frying pan. Freeze cooled akara for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Akara, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous platter of West African black-eyed pea fritters with extra peas, warm ginger and a deeply golden crust. The larger batch makes a substantial savoury snack.

steps.instruction: Pat the cowpeas dry so the larger fritter batter stays thick.
Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic into pieces small enough for the blender.
Blend the cowpeas, onion, bell pepper, garlic, ginger, cayenne pepper, water and salt into a thick, slightly textured batter.
Beat the batter vigorously until it becomes airy and holds soft peaks.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Fry generous spoonfuls of batter until deeply golden and cooked through, working in batches.
Drain the akara briefly on absorbent paper.
Rest the akara until the crust finishes setting and the centre is safe to eat.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten warm. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a hot oven or dry pan until crisp. Freeze cooked akara for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Chicken and mushroom congee, light
recipes.summary: Silky Chinese rice porridge with tender chicken, mushrooms, ginger and softly cooked egg. Extra broth and mushrooms keep the gluten-free breakfast generous but light.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the chicken thigh, mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms, ginger, garlic and spring onions.
Heat the sesame oil in a deep saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the ginger and garlic until fragrant without allowing the garlic to brown.
Add the chicken broth, white rice and salt and bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
Simmer the congee until the rice begins to break down and the broth turns silky.
Add the chicken thigh and simmer until the thigh pieces are cooked through.
Add the mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms and simmer until tender.
Crack the eggs into the congee and cook until the whites are set and the yolks remain tender.
Finish the chicken and mushroom congee with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat with extra chicken broth because the rice thickens while stored. Freezing is not recommended because the eggs and mushrooms lose texture.

recipes.title: Chicken and mushroom congee
recipes.summary: Comforting Chinese congee simmered until creamy with chicken, two kinds of mushrooms, ginger and eggs. It is a warm, savoury and naturally gluten-free breakfast.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the chicken thigh, mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms, ginger, garlic and spring onions.
Heat the sesame oil in a deep saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the ginger and garlic until fragrant without allowing the garlic to brown.
Add the chicken broth, white rice and salt and bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
Simmer the congee until the rice breaks down and the broth becomes creamy.
Add the chicken thigh and simmer until every thigh piece is cooked through.
Add the mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms and simmer until tender.
Crack the eggs into the congee and cook until the whites are set and the yolks are softly cooked.
Finish the chicken and mushroom congee with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and loosen with chicken broth during reheating. Heat until steaming throughout. The finished congee is not ideal for freezing.

recipes.title: Chicken and mushroom congee, hearty
recipes.summary: A substantial Chinese breakfast porridge with extra rice, chicken and eggs, plus plenty of mushrooms. Ginger and sesame oil give the creamy congee a warm savoury finish.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the chicken thigh, mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms, ginger, garlic and spring onions.
Heat the sesame oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the ginger and garlic until fragrant without allowing the garlic to brown.
Add the chicken broth, white rice and salt and bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
Simmer the congee until the larger amount of rice is very soft and the broth is thick and silky.
Add the chicken thigh and simmer until every piece is tender and cooked through.
Add the mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms and simmer until completely tender.
Crack the eggs into the congee and cook until the whites are set and the yolks reach your preferred consistency.
Finish the chicken and mushroom congee generously with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat with additional chicken broth until steaming. Freezing is not recommended because the eggs and mushrooms change texture.

recipes.title: Poulet à la crème, light
recipes.summary: Tender chicken breast and mushrooms in a light French cream sauce with thyme, spinach and lemon. Extra vegetables keep the keto lunch generous without relying on starch.

steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken breast, mushrooms, spinach, onion and garlic before heating the pan.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken breast in batches until golden outside but not fully cooked within.
Transfer the breast pieces to a plate and keep them nearby.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in the remaining butter until the mushrooms are golden and dry at the edges.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and simmer until reduced by about one third.
Return the chicken breast to the pan and simmer until the breast is cooked through.
Stir in the heavy cream and salt and simmer until the sauce lightly coats the chicken.
Fold in the spinach and cook until just wilted.
Finish the poulet à la crème with the lemon juice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently over low heat so the cream sauce does not split. Freeze for up to 1 month, though the sauce may need whisking after thawing.

recipes.title: Poulet à la crème
recipes.summary: Classic French-style chicken and mushrooms simmered in a rich cream and thyme sauce. Spinach and lemon bring freshness to the deeply savoury keto lunch.

steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken thigh, mushrooms, spinach, onion and garlic before heating the pan.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken thigh in batches until golden outside but not fully cooked within.
Transfer the thigh pieces to a plate and keep them nearby.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in the remaining butter until the mushrooms are deeply golden.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and simmer until reduced by about one third.
Return the chicken thigh to the pan and simmer until the thigh is tender and cooked through.
Stir in the heavy cream and salt and simmer until the sauce is rich and spoonable.
Fold in the spinach and cook until wilted.
Finish the poulet à la crème with the lemon juice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently without boiling. Freeze for up to 1 month; stir the sauce well after thawing and reheating.

recipes.title: Poulet à la crème, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous French pan of chicken, mushrooms and spinach in a rich thyme cream sauce. Extra chicken and cream make this a substantial high-protein keto lunch for four.

steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken thigh, mushrooms, spinach, onion and garlic before heating the pan.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken thigh in batches until deeply golden outside.
Transfer the thigh pieces to a plate and keep them nearby.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in the remaining butter until the mushrooms are deeply browned.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and simmer until reduced by about one third.
Return the chicken thigh to the pan and simmer until tender and cooked through.
Stir in the heavy cream and salt and simmer until the sauce becomes thick and glossy.
Fold in the spinach and cook until evenly wilted.
Finish the poulet à la crème with the lemon juice.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheat slowly over low heat. Freeze for up to 1 month, then thaw overnight and whisk the sauce while reheating.

recipes.title: Greek lemon chicken traybake, light
recipes.summary: Roasted lemon-garlic chicken with potatoes, zucchini and onion in a thyme-scented pan sauce. Extra zucchini and less oil keep this Mediterranean dinner lighter.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C so the traybake begins roasting immediately.
Prepare the chicken breast, potato, zucchini and onion in their listed sizes.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, chicken stock, thyme, paprika and salt together.
Arrange the potato and onion in a large roasting tray and coat them with half the lemon mixture.
Roast the potato and onion until they begin to soften and colour at the edges.
Add the chicken breast and zucchini to the tray and coat them with the remaining lemon mixture.
Roast until the breast is cooked through, the zucchini is tender and the potato is golden.
Rest the Greek lemon chicken traybake so the pan juices settle around the vegetables.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat covered until the chicken is hot throughout. Freeze for up to 2 months, though the zucchini will soften after thawing.

recipes.title: Greek lemon chicken traybake
recipes.summary: Greek-style chicken thighs roasted with potatoes, zucchini, onion, garlic and plenty of lemon. The vegetables absorb the savoury thyme-scented pan juices.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C so the traybake begins roasting immediately.
Prepare the chicken thigh, potato, zucchini and onion in their listed sizes.

Arrange the potato and onion in a large roasting tray and coat them with half the lemon mixture.
Roast the potato and onion until they begin to soften and turn golden.
Add the chicken thigh and zucchini to the tray and coat them with the remaining lemon mixture.
Roast until the thigh is tender, the zucchini is soft and the potato is deeply golden.

recipes.title: Greek lemon chicken traybake, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Greek traybake with extra chicken thighs and potatoes in a rich lemon, garlic and olive oil sauce. Zucchini and onion keep the substantial dinner colourful.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C so the larger traybake begins roasting immediately.
Prepare the chicken thigh, potato, zucchini and onion in their listed sizes.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, chicken stock, thyme, paprika and salt together.
Arrange the potato and onion across two roasting trays and coat them with half the lemon mixture.
Roast the potato and onion until they begin to soften and brown at the edges.
Add the chicken thigh and zucchini to the trays and coat them with the remaining lemon mixture.
Roast until the thigh is tender and the potato is crisp and deeply golden.
Rest the Greek lemon chicken traybake so the rich pan juices settle.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat covered until piping hot. Freeze in portions for up to 2 months, accepting that the zucchini will be softer.

recipes.title: Moroccan chicken skewers, light
recipes.summary: Grilled chicken breast marinated with yogurt, lemon, cumin, paprika, ginger and garlic. Crisp cucumber keeps this high-protein North African snack fresh and light.

steps.instruction: Cut the chicken breast and cucumber and prepare the garlic, ginger and cilantro.
Stir the greek yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, cumin, paprika, olive oil and salt together.
Coat the chicken breast with the yogurt mixture until every piece is covered.
Marinate the chicken breast in the refrigerator so the spices flavour the meat.
Thread the chicken breast pieces onto skewers with small gaps between them.
Heat the grill until very hot before adding the skewers.
Grill the chicken skewers until browned outside and cooked through at the centre.
Rest the Moroccan chicken skewers so the breast stays juicy.
Serve the skewers with the cucumber and cilantro.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served freshly grilled. Refrigerate cooked skewers for up to 3 days and reheat gently. Keep the cucumber separate. Freeze cooked chicken for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Moroccan chicken skewers
recipes.summary: Juicy Moroccan-style chicken skewers with a yogurt, lemon, cumin, paprika and ginger marinade. Cucumber and cilantro make them a lively high-protein snack.

Coat the chicken breast with the yogurt mixture until every piece is evenly covered.
Marinate the chicken breast in the refrigerator so the lemon and spices penetrate the meat.
Thread the chicken breast pieces onto skewers with small gaps between them.

Rest the Moroccan chicken skewers so the breast pieces remain juicy.
Serve the skewers with the cucumber and cilantro.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate cooked skewers for up to 3 days and reheat gently until hot. Keep the cucumber separate. Freeze the cooked chicken for up to 2 months.
